chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Khalid, from his father, who raised it (mursal) and said:

The Jews gathered around their chief, al-Jalut, and said to him, 'This man is learned' — meaning Amir al-Mu'minin (peace be upon him) — 'so come with us to him that we may question him.' So they came to him, and it was said to them, 'He is in the palace.' So they waited for him until he came out.
Then the chief of al-Jalut said to him, 'We came to question you.' So he (Imam Ali) said, 'Ask, O Jew, about whatever comes to you.' So he said, 'I ask you about your Lord — when was He?'

He said: 'He was without there being any entities. He was without a how. He has always been without an extent and without a how. He was — there being no before for Him. He is before the before, without a before, and no end-point, and no termination. The end-point is cut off from Him, and He is the end-point of every end-point.'
Then the chief of al-Jalut said, 'Let us go, for he is more knowledgeable than what is said about him.'

key_terms.رأس الجالوت: Ras al-Jalut — the Jewish Exilarch, head of the Jewish community in Babylonia under Abbasid rule
key_terms.غاية كل غاية: End-point of every end-point — God is the ultimate boundary of all limits
key_terms.قبل القبل: Before the before — God precedes even the concept of anteriority itself
key_terms.كمّ: Kamm — quantity, extent; God has no measurable extent
key_terms.كيف: Kayf — qualitative state, modality; God transcends all categories of how
key_terms.كيفنونية: Kaynaniyya — the state of entities existing alongside God; pre-creational plurality

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali say to the Jewish Exilarch about the nature and eternity of God?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a dialogue between the Jewish Exilarch (Ras al-Jalut) and Imam Ali (AS) about the nature of God's pre-eternity. When asked 'when was God?', Imam Ali responded with a profound apophatic theological statement: God exists beyond all categories of time, space, quality, quantity, and causality. He preceded all 'befores', has no end-point, and is Himself the ultimate end-point of every limit. The Exilarch's astonished concession demonstrates the transcendence of Imami theological insight over conventional religious discourse.
word_analysis: there being any entities/existence alongside Him
